name: Gal
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Only Z'graggen wordlists/surveys (1969, 1975, 1980) in Glottolog for Gal (gap); no phonology or grammar

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid page gall1278 + bib records 589056 (Pick 2020, A Reconstruction of Proto-Northern Adelbert Phonology and Lexicon, PhD UH Manoa) and 302422 (Pawley & Hammarstrom 2017, The Trans New Guinea family)
sources.note: Zero grammar/sketch/phonology refs for Gal; Pick 2020 and Pawley & Hammarstrom 2017 are cited for subclassification only (Pick's language list does not include Gal).

sources.citation: Z'graggen, J. A. 1980. A comparative word list of the Mabuso languages, Madang Province, Papua New Guinea. Pacific Linguistics D-32. Canberra: ANU. DOI 10.15144/PL-D32
sources.note: Gal = list C27 (Baimak C25 separate). Intro sec. 6 pp. viii-ix: 'The transcription is semi-phonemic'; only a segment-fluctuation note for Gal. No occurrence of stress/accent/tone/pitch anywhere in the volume; forms unmarked for stress (visual check pp. 2-3).

sources.citation: Z'graggen, J. A. 1971. Classificatory and typological studies in languages of the Madang District. Pacific Linguistics C-19. Canberra: ANU. DOI 10.15144/PL-C19 (open scan via sealang.net/archives/pl/pdf/)
sources.note: Sec. 1.3.3, p. 6 (verified on page image): 'The marking of stress has been omitted, since the stress patterning has not been well established yet.' -- covers the whole survey incl. Gal (language 82 'Gl'). Sec. 2.21.12.20 p. 30 Gal: villages; 'Capell (1969) collected some firsthand notes.' Sec. 2.21.16 Mabuso typological features: segmental/morphological only, nothing prosodic.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, John A. 1969. Classificatory and typological studies in languages of the (Western) Madang District, New Guinea. PhD thesis, Australian National University. hdl 1885/130077
sources.note: pp. 13-14: same sentence -- stress marking omitted because stress patterning not yet established. Gal = 82/Gl, Mabuso.
Stub; its PARADISEC 'notes about the grammar of Gal' link is Capell collection item INHALM202 (Halmahera) = Galela, a misattribution, not this language.

sources.note: Nothing; gazetteer only (villages Gal 1 pop. 96, Gal 2 pop. 74, Sanepi 54 = C27 Gal).
Nothing; sole source is Z'graggen (1980) lexicon.
